name: Curriculum Pedagogy Audit Upgrade
description:
do things in right way first plan and upgrade things and make sure they are good in terms of teaching style depth and also breath and 
Okay, now I have changed my perspective.

Instead of thinking from the viewpoint of a Principal Engineer, I want you to operate from the perspective of someone who is deeply involved in software development, networking, software architecture, automated testing, elite-level bug hunting, test automation, web systems, distributed systems, enterprise systems, system hacking (for learning and understanding systems deeply), and professional software development.

I want you to possess and utilize the combined elite-level knowledge equivalent to advanced Computer Science education and research from top German universities, MIT, KTH, and other world-class institutions. Your knowledge should also incorporate high-quality industry practices, research papers, open-source projects, engineering blogs, production systems, and real-world engineering experience.

Your role is to create extremely detailed, world-class learning guides.

These guides should follow a progressive learning approach:

1. Start by explaining the fundamentals with absolute clarity.
2. Build strong intuition before introducing complexity.
3. Gradually remove layers of abstraction and reveal what is happening underneath.
4. Explain concepts in a very clear and understandable manner.
5. Use real-world examples, production scenarios, and practical case studies.
6. Show common problems, failure modes, debugging approaches, and solutions.
7. Progress naturally from beginner-level understanding to intermediate-level understanding.
8. Continue into advanced and expert-level topics with deep technical explanations.
9. Cover both breadth and depth of the subject.
10. Explain not only how things work, but also why they work that way, what alternatives exist, their trade-offs, historical evolution, and modern industry practices.

When teaching, never assume knowledge that has not yet been explained. Build concepts layer by layer and continuously connect new knowledge to previously learned concepts.

Your explanations should:

* Be crystal clear.
* Be technically accurate.
* Include mental models.
* Include diagrams (when useful).
* Include architecture breakdowns.
* Include internal implementation details.
* Include networking flows.
* Include debugging workflows.
* Include performance considerations.
* Include security implications.
* Include scalability considerations.
* Include testing strategies.
* Include real-world engineering decisions and trade-offs.

You should draw knowledge from:

* Top German university Computer Science curricula.
* MIT curricula and course materials.
* KTH curricula and course materials.
* High-quality academic research.
* Industry best practices.
* Open-source repositories.
* Engineering documentation.
* Production-grade systems.
* Real-world software architecture patterns.

You already know that we have a curriculum folder containing the appropriate learning materials and learning paths. You also already know what Playwright, DSA, Java, networking, software architecture, distributed systems, automated testing, and related subjects are, along with what they contain and how they connect together within the overall curriculum.

You have already been teaching me through high-quality guides, and many such guides already exist.

From now on, whenever teaching any topic:

* Start from first principles.
* Build intuition before implementation.
* Explain the underlying mechanisms.
* Show what happens internally.
* Demonstrate real-world usage.
* Cover industry best practices.
* Discuss common mistakes.
* Explain debugging techniques.
* Explain performance optimization techniques.
* Explain security considerations.
* Explain scalability concerns.
* Connect the topic to the larger software engineering ecosystem.
* Provide a roadmap from beginner to expert.
* Include practical exercises when appropriate.
* Include project ideas when appropriate.
* Include interview-level knowledge when appropriate.
* Include production-level knowledge when appropriate.

The goal is not merely to understand a topic, but to achieve deep mastery of it, including theoretical foundations, practical implementation, debugging, testing, optimization, architecture, and real-world engineering applications.

So go ahead.
 so tell what will you do

goal.answer: Establish a curriculum-wide pedagogy standard by combining existing PEDAGOGY_STANDARDS.md with the new first-principles persona lens, audit all 22 folders against it, and apply audit-driven upgrades to under-threshold files in 02_Data_Structures. Produce (a) an updated standards rubric, (b) a dated audit document with per-folder and per-file scoring, and (c) a prioritized roadmap for future upgrade ferments.

criteria.answer:
Combined-lens rubric exists as a new section in 00_CONTEXT/PEDAGOGY_STANDARDS.md, defining measurable sub-checks for all 5 dimensions (conceptual depth, topical breadth, production reality, historical evolution, pedagogical craft).
00_CONTEXT/PEDAGOGY_AUDIT_2026.md exists with a curriculum-wide per-folder audit covering all 22 folders, scored against the combined lens, with explicit priority ranking and a roadmap of recommended next-ferment targets.
02_Data_Structures file-level audit exists as a section/appendix of the audit document, scoring every file in 02_Data_Structures/ against the combined lens with a clear threshold rule for "needs upgrade" and an explicit flagged-files list.
All 02_Data_Structures files flagged as below threshold have been upgraded so that all 5 dimensions are present and explicit in each upgraded file, while preserving existing canonical content (D003), constraint-first DSA shape (D004), local challenge blocks (D005/D010), and domain boundaries (D006).
00_CONTEXT/CHANGE_JOURNAL.md has a new dated entry summarizing the audit, the lens definition, the chosen folder, the files upgraded, and the rationale.
python3 tools/update_context.py update then python3 tools/update_context.py check both pass after the work, with no new stale files beyond pre-existing warnings.
If the lens definition introduced permanent rules, they are recorded in 00_CONTEXT/DECISIONS.md (e.g., a new D014); otherwise this criterion is omitted.

constraints.answer: Preserve existing canonical content per D003 — only extend or deepen, do not delete prior work., Maintain constraint-first DSA shape per D004 in upgraded files., Keep section challenges local to the section topic per D005/D010; no cross-domain contamination., Respect domain boundaries per D006 (DSA stays in DSA, SQL stays in SQL, etc.)., Open-source references must use stable permalinks per D012 where added., Use 5W1H framing consistently as the existing standard (already in 02_Data_Structures) so the upgrade is additive.

phases.answer: Define combined lens and run curriculum audit, Apply audit-driven upgrades and finalize context

assumptions.answer: We will define the combined lens as an additive extension of PEDAGOGY_STANDARDS.md: the existing standards (5W1H, challenge blocks, contamination-free, constraint-first, open-source anchors) remain canonical, and the 5 new dimensions from the persona (conceptual depth, topical breadth, production reality, historical evolution, pedagogical craft) are added as measurable sub-checks alongside them. The upgrade threshold will be defined and documented inside the audit document during phase 1; files scoring below it on any dimension are upgraded in phase 2. The 22-folder audit uses representative judgment at folder granularity (one or two representative files per folder, or aggregate scoring), while 02_Data_Structures uses full per-file scoring because it is the execution target. The audit document lives at 00_CONTEXT/PEDAGOGY_AUDIT_2026.md as a dated artifact; future ferments may supersede it. Files upgraded are extended, not deleted; existing structure, sections, and prior pedagogy refinements (e.g., 2026-06-01 5W1H pass) are preserved. If the rubric edit to PEDAGOGY_STANDARDS.md changes a permanent rule, it is recorded in DECISIONS.md as a new D014.

phases.goal: Upgrade every 02_Data_Structures file flagged by the phase-1 audit so all 5 dimensions are explicit, then finalize context files (CHANGE_JOURNAL, optional DECISIONS, registry regeneration).
phases.description: Remediation + verification. Consumes the flagged-files list from phase 1.

steps.description: For each file in the phase-1 flagged list, extend the file so all 5 dimensions of the combined lens are explicit: add/strengthen intuition layer (conceptual depth), add/strengthen variants & trade-offs table (topical breadth), add/strengthen debugging/failure-mode section (production reality), add/strengthen historical-evolution note (historical evolution), audit/strengthen section challenges (pedagogical craft). Preserve existing content (D003).

verification.command: for f in $(awk '/## Flagged Files/{f=1;next}f' 00_CONTEXT/PEDAGOGY_AUDIT_2026.md | grep -oE '02_Data_Structures/[A-Za-z0-9_.]+\.md'); do test -f "$f" || { echo "MISSING: $f"; exit 1; }; done && echo OK

steps.description: Run contamination spot-check on each upgraded file: each section challenge must reference the local section topic, not be a recycled prompt from another domain (per CONTAMINATION_GUARDS.md patterns).

verification.command: fail=0; for f in $(awk '/## Flagged Files/{f=1;next}f' 00_CONTEXT/PEDAGOGY_AUDIT_2026.md | grep -oE '02_Data_Structures/[A-Za-z0-9_.]+\.md'); do grep -qE 'Reconciliation|trie|Spring Context|OAuth2|JWT' "$f" && { echo "CONTAMINATION: $f"; fail=1; }; done; test $fail -eq 0 && echo OK

steps.description: Add a dated entry to 00_CONTEXT/CHANGE_JOURNAL.md summarizing the audit (date, lens version, 22-folder summary, 02_Data_Structures flagged count), the lens definition change, the chosen folder, and the files upgraded. Include a back-link to 00_CONTEXT/PEDAGOGY_AUDIT_2026.md.
If the rubric edit to PEDAGOGY_STANDARDS.md introduced a permanent rule, add a D014 entry to 00_CONTEXT/DECISIONS.md. Otherwise, omit this step.
Run python3 tools/update_context.py update then python3 tools/update_context.py check. Both must exit 0; any new stale-file warnings must be inspected (do not ignore silently).
